{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software licence, hosting and MarketSite.net agreement  
**Status:** 19 rules assessed — 12 compliant, 6 deviations, 1 missing

---

## 1. Executive summary

On balance this is a favourable paper for us. The commercial framework carries no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum purchase commitment, no non-solicit and no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; the audit right in Section 4.4 is at the preferred position (annual cap, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, Vendor-borne costs with a 5% underpayment shift, no systems access); assignment is mutual with an express M&A carve-out for us; renewal is annual on 30 days' notice; and governing law sits at the fallback (California law, San Francisco-seated AAA arbitration).

The Vendor IP indemnity in Section 8 is strong and, because Section 9 excepts Section 8 from both the cap and the consequential-damages waiver, it is uncapped and one-way in our favour. Nothing there needs narrowing.

Six items require negotiation, two of which we treat as walk-away issues. First, the Section 9 cap is not twelve months' fees but only amounts actually paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to," which slices the cap to a single transaction's fees and leaves confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct inside the cap. Second, the exit provisions in Section 11.3 permit destruction of our data at the Vendor's election, with no return obligation, format, deadline or certification. Alongside those, Section 13.5 assigns ownership of Developments we create back to the Vendor wherever the Vendor supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back; the Section 2 licences do not reach our affiliates or contractors; there is no customer termination-for-convenience right in a five-year term; the product warranty period expires 60 days from the Effective Date (hard-capped at 31 December 1999) and can lapse on or before acceptance; and there is no Vendor insurance obligation anywhere in the document.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs) | **Deviation** | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 INDEMNIFICATION. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant (fallback) | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4 FEES. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | PRICING |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4 FEES. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. |

### Deviation detail and proposed positions

- **§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES (IP, critical).** Section 13.5 correctly gives us ownership of Developments created solely by us, but the "unless supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" carve-out transfers ownership of our own work product to the Vendor with no licence back. That fails both the preferred and the fallback position. *Proposal:* delete the carve-out only, leaving the Vendor's pre-existing materials and Section 2.8 Software ownership untouched; if ongoing support is the real concern, a support licence to the Vendor is the sensible fallback. Noted, not flagged: ownership of Software enhancements is left to future negotiation and there is no Customer Data ownership sentence (the Agreement has no Customer Data concept).

- **§ 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY (LOL-CAP, critical).** The clause is mutual in form and carves Section 8 out of both the cap and the consequential-damages waiver, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: the cap is limited to amounts actually paid for the single "transaction which the liability relates to" in the prior twelve months, and the only carve-out is Section 8 — confidentiality (Section 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap. *Proposal:* mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, measured from the event giving rise to liability, plus an "Excluded Claims" definition covering Section 8 indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud. The mutual consequential-damages exclusion stays. *Drafting note:* p0092 appears to be an OCR duplicate across a page break; conform to the edited p0090.

- **§ 3 GRANT OF RIGHTS (LICENSE, high).** The grant is perpetual and irrevocable and Section 14.1 satisfies the fallback on transferability, but affiliates and contractors are nowhere addressed ("Affiliate" does not appear in the Agreement) and there is no mechanism to add them, failing the fallback. *Proposal:* new Section 2.11 extending the Section 2 licences to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, with us responsible for their compliance. "Corio Servers" ("owned or operated by or for Corio") addresses contractor use only in part.

- **§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION (T4C, high).** We have no convenience right during the five-year initial term — Section 11.1 permits only non-renewal, Section 11.2 only breach or insolvency. *Proposal:* insert a Corio convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid recurring fees and no early-termination penalty, and confirm no Vendor convenience right during the term (the Vendor's lack of a mid-term right is acceptable to us). Insert after 11.2; existing 11.3 renumbers.

- **§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION (TRANSITION, medium).** Continuity is better than preferred (Sections 11.3 and 5.3 survive termination for then-existing Customers, plus Section 12 escrow), but there is no data return: Section 11.3 allows "return or destroy" at the Vendor's election, with no obligation covering our, our Customers' or Software Users' data on the MarketSite.net Service, no machine-readable format, no deadline and no deletion certification. *Proposal:* new Section 11.4 requiring return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification, plus six months' transition assistance at then-current rates (90 days acceptable as fallback).

- **§ 8 / 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER (WARRANTY, medium).** Sections 7.3–7.4 contain a genuine conformance, media and no-malicious-code warranty with correction, replacement and refund remedies, and the disclaimer does not swallow them. The failure is duration: 60 days from the Effective Date, hard-capped at 31 December 1999, while Acceptance Testing under Section 3.1 may itself run to 31 December 1999 — so the warranty can expire on or before acceptance, below the 90-day software fallback. *Proposal:* twelve months from acceptance (preferred); 90 days from acceptance acceptable. Remedies and exclusions untouched.

- **§ 14 MISCELLANEOUS (INSURANCE, low — missing).** No insurance obligation exists; the sole use of "insurance" is an accounting exclusion in the Net Revenue definition. Absence of any coverage for a vendor whose service touches Customer data fails even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). *Proposal:* insert the preferred coverage package as new Section 14.10 and renumber Complete Understanding to 14.11.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Transaction-limited liability cap (§ 9).** A cap measured only against the fees paid for the single related transaction can fall well below six months' fees — walk-away territory for a vendor cap. We need the mutual twelve-month/USD 1,000,000 floor and the Excluded Claims carve-outs.
2. **Vendor election to destroy our data on exit (§ 11.3).** Wording that permits outright destruction with no return right is walk-away territory. We need return within 30 days in machine-readable format before any deletion, with certification.

The Section 13.5 ownership carve-out is not labelled walk-away but is a critical deviation: it assigns IP we create to the Vendor with no licence back, and we should treat it as non-negotiable in substance.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the six deviations and the missing insurance clause, prefixing each comment with **[Playbook]** and citing the playbook position and fallback.
2. Lead the negotiation on the two walk-away items (§ 9 cap and carve-outs; § 11 data return) and on § 13.5 ownership; hold the § 2 affiliate/contractor extension, § 11 convenience right and § 7 warranty duration as the second tier, where the stated fallbacks (support licence to Vendor; 90 days' transition assistance; 90 days' warranty from acceptance) give us landing zones.
3. Confirm with the business the operational impact of the five-year term without a convenience right, and the identity of the affiliates and contractors that need licence coverage.
4. Ask the Vendor for current certificates of insurance in support of the new Section 14.10.
5. On conforming the execution copy, reconcile the apparent OCR duplication at p0092 against the edited § 9 text at p0090, and renumber § 11.3 and § 14.10 as noted.
6. No action required on the compliant items; we will not spend capital on the noted sub-preferred mechanics (renewal reminder and price-uplift cap, "reasonable notice" in § 4.4, California law and arbitral forum, absence of an express affiliate carve-out and "not unreasonably withheld" qualifier in § 14.1).
"}
